info.title: API do Financeiro Inteligente
info.description:
Você que é dev, divirta-se! ✨

> **Índice da documentação** — acesse o índice completo em [https://docs.finance.kobana.com.br/llms.txt](https://docs.finance.kobana.com.br/llms.txt). Use este arquivo para descobrir todas as páginas disponíveis antes de explorar.

## Autenticação

Toda requisição precisa de **duas** coisas: o token, que diz qual **organização** você é, e o cabeçalho `X-Workspace-Id`, que diz em qual **espaço de trabalho** dela agir.

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-Workspace-Id: <uuid do espaço de trabalho>
```

### O token

Bearer JWT assinado em **RS256** pelo servidor de autorização da Kobana (HS512 apenas contra um servidor de desenvolvimento local).

| Claim | Papel |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`org`** | **O tenant.** O `public_id` da organização — é o que decide quais dados o token alcança. |
| `sub` | A **pessoa** que autorizou. Não escolhe dados, mas limita o que o token faz às permissões dela na organização (ver abaixo). |
| `scope` | Lista separada por espaços de escopos `finance/<recurso>` (o alcance) e níveis de acesso (os verbos), ex.: `finance/payables finance/people read write` — ver [Escopos e níveis de acesso](#escopos-e-níveis-de-acesso). |
| `jti` | Identificador do token, usado para revogação. |
| `iss` / `aud` / `exp` | Emissor, destinatário e expiração. |

⚠️ O tenant é `org`, nunca `sub`. São espaços de identificadores diferentes: um id de pessoa jamais corresponde a uma organização, então um token montado com o valor errado falha em toda requisição.

### Escopos e níveis de acesso

Uma requisição exige **um verbo**, dado pelo método HTTP, sobre **o recurso** que o endpoint nomeia:

| Método | Nível de acesso exigido |
| :--- | :--- |
| `GET` | `read` (também concedido por `write` ou `all`) |
| `POST`, `PATCH`, `PUT` | `write` (ou `all`) — mandar pagamento ao banco e emitir cobrança inclusive |
| `DELETE` | `delete` (ou `all`) — `write` não exclui |

O servidor de autorização emite seis níveis de acesso: `read`, `write`, `delete`, `import`, `export` e `all`. Um não substitui o outro; `all` concede todos. `import` e `export` são para endpoints em lote — esta API não tem nenhum hoje.

Um token tem uma de duas formas:

- **Só o nível de acesso** (sem escopo `finance/…`): o nível sozinho decide, em todo recurso.
- **Com escopos `finance/<recurso>`** (o de um cliente OAuth — um cliente MCP, por exemplo — ou um token pessoal limitado a alguns recursos): os recursos definem o alcance e os níveis só valem dentro dele. `finance/payables read write` lê e escreve contas a pagar e nada mais; `finance/all` alcança todo recurso, mas sozinho não concede verbo nenhum.

Cada operação declara o que exige como "Requires scope `finance/<recurso>` with access level `<nível>`". Mover dinheiro é `write` no recurso próprio: mandar ao banco e cancelar o envio exigem `finance/payable_dispatches`; emitir e cancelar uma cobrança exigem `finance/receivable_charges` — um token que só alcança `finance/payables` não manda ao banco. `GET /me` não exige escopo: use-o para testar um token.

> **Mudou:** os escopos antigos `finance.<recurso>`, `finance.<recurso>.write` e `finance.all` não são mais aceitos; um `DELETE` exige `delete` (`write` não exclui mais); mover dinheiro exige `write`, não `all`; e desvincular um anexo passou de `DELETE /attachments/{id}/links` para `POST /attachments/{id}/unlink`.

### Permissões da pessoa

O escopo é o teto do **aplicativo**, decidido no consentimento. Quando o `sub` é uma pessoa que já entrou no Finance, a API também cobra dela a **mesma permissão** que a ação exige no dashboard: um token com `finance/payables` e `write` de alguém que só pode listar contas a pagar não cria uma. Membros suspensos, pendentes ou removidos não alcançam nada, e a pessoa precisa ter acesso ao espaço do `X-Workspace-Id`. Um token cujo `sub` não é membro da organização (um token de sistema) continua limitado só pelos escopos.

### O cabeçalho `X-Workspace-Id`

Uma organização pode ter **vários espaços de trabalho**, e toda rota desta API responde por exatamente **um**. O token sozinho não diz qual — por isso o cabeçalho é obrigatório em todas as operações.

Ele é um **seletor, nunca uma permissão**: o espaço informado é conferido contra a organização do token. Um espaço que pertence a outra organização responde exatamente como um que não existe — de propósito, para a resposta não revelar que aquele id é real em outro lugar.

| Situação | Resposta |
| :--- | :--- |
| Cabeçalho ausente | `400` `WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` |
| Espaço de outra organização, inexistente, ou id malformado | `403` `UNKNOWN_WORKSPACE` |
| `org` não corresponde a nenhuma organização | `403` `UNKNOWN_ORGANIZATION` |
| A organização do token está suspensa ou inativa | `403` `ORGANIZATION_SUSPENDED` |
| Escopo insuficiente para a operação | `403` `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` |
| Uma regra de Segurança do espaço barrou a operação (`details.reason` diz qual) | `403` `SECURITY_BLOCKED` |
| O espaço não tem plano contratado e a operação é de uso efetivo — enviar ao banco, emitir cobrança (`details.reason` = `no_plan`) | `403` `ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED` |
| A pessoa do token não tem a permissão que a operação exige (`details.required` diz qual) | `403` `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION` |
| A pessoa do token não é membro da organização, ou está suspensa, pendente, removida ou sem permissão nenhuma nela | `403` `MEMBERSHIP_INACTIVE` |
| A pessoa do token não tem acesso a este espaço de trabalho | `403` `WORKSPACE_ACCESS_DENIED` |

### Exemplo

```bash
curl https://api.finance.kobana.com.br/v1/payables \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KOBANA_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Workspace-Id: $KOBANA_WORKSPACE_ID"
```

Para testes em linha de comando, exporte os dois: `export KOBANA_TOKEN=xxxxxxxx` e `export KOBANA_WORKSPACE_ID=xxxxxxxx`, e cole os comandos da documentação no terminal.

## Formato

A API aceita apenas o formato `JSON`. Todas as requisições devem usar `Content-Type: application/json`. Todas as respostas usam `snake_case`.

| Tipo de Campo | Formato |
| :--- | :--- |
| **DateTime** | Formato [ISO8601](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601). Exemplos — Data: `2026-01-24`. Data e Hora: `2026-01-24T10:07:00.000Z` |
| **Money** | Decimal como string com 2 casas (`"150.00"`). Sempre positivo — direção indicada pelo campo `type` (`debit`/`credit`) ou pelo contexto (payable/receivable). |
| **UUID** | Identificadores de recursos no formato UUID v4 |

## Convenções

Convenções usadas nesta documentação:

| Convenção | Descrição |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`:id`** | Parâmetro de path que deve ser substituído pelo UUID do recurso. |
| **`#{variable}`** | Valor da sua conta que deve ser substituído no exemplo. |
| **`...`** | Conteúdo da resposta truncado para facilitar a leitura. |
| **`$KOBANA_TOKEN`** | Token JWT de acesso. Exporte com `export KOBANA_TOKEN=xxxxxxxx`. |
| **`$KOBANA_WORKSPACE_ID`** | UUID do espaço de trabalho, enviado em `X-Workspace-Id`. Exporte com `export KOBANA_WORKSPACE_ID=xxxxxxxx`. |

## Ambientes

| Ambiente | Base URL |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Produção** | `https://api.finance.kobana.com.br/v1` |
| **Sandbox** | `https://api.finance.sandbox.kobana.com.br/v1` |

## Códigos de Retorno

A API retorna códigos HTTP padrão:

| | Código | Descrição |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ✅ | **200 OK** | Requisição bem-sucedida com corpo de resposta. |
| ✅ | **201 Created** | Recurso criado com sucesso. |
| ✅ | **204 No Content** | Requisição bem-sucedida, sem corpo de resposta. |
| ❌ | **400 Bad Request** | Requisição inválida — conteúdo mal formado, filtro não permitido, ou `X-Workspace-Id` ausente. |
| ❌ | **401 Unauthorized** | Token ausente, inválido ou expirado. |
| ❌ | **403 Forbidden** | Escopo ou permissão insuficiente, organização desconhecida, ou espaço de trabalho fora dela. |
| ❌ | **404 Not Found** | Recurso não encontrado ou fora do workspace. |
| ❌ | **422 Unprocessable Entity** | Requisição válida, mas os dados enviados não são. |
| ❌ | **429 Too Many Requests** | Limite de requisições atingido. |
| ❌ | **500 Internal Server Error** | Erro interno no processamento. Consulte o [status dos servidores](https://status.kobana.com.br). |

## Listagem e Paginação

Todos os endpoints de listagem usam **paginação por cursor**:

```
GET /v1/payables?cursor=<opaque_cursor>&limit=25
```

A resposta inclui `meta.next_cursor` — passe-o como `?cursor=` na próxima requisição para buscar a página seguinte. Quando `meta.next_cursor` é `null`, não há mais páginas.

## Idempotência

Operações de criação (`POST`) aceitam o cabeçalho `X-Idempotency-Key`. Reenvios com a mesma chave retornam o resultado original sem criar duplicatas — seguro para retry em caso de falha de rede.

```
X-Idempotency-Key: <uuid-v4-gerado-pelo-cliente>
```

## ID das Requisições (Request ID)

Cada requisição possui um identificador associado, disponível no cabeçalho `Request-Id` da resposta. Esse valor ajuda na depuração e auditoria. O log de requisições fica disponível por **30 dias**. Ao abrir um chamado de suporte sobre uma requisição específica, informe o `Request-Id` para acelerar a investigação.

## Segurança

A API usa certificados **SSL 2048 bits**. Toda requisição deve ser feita via **HTTPS** — chamadas na porta 80 são redirecionadas para 443.

Os clientes devem suportar `TLSv1.2` ou `TLSv1.3` com uma das cifras: `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`, `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`, `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384`, `ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384`. `TLSv1` e `TLSv1.1` não são suportados.

## Cache HTTP

Use os cabeçalhos HTTP de cache para reduzir carga e ganhar velocidade. A maioria das respostas inclui `ETag` e/ou `Last-Modified` — armazene esses valores e reenvie nas próximas requisições via `If-None-Match` e `If-Modified-Since`. Se o recurso não mudou, a resposta será `304 Not Modified`, sem corpo e sem reprocessamento.

## Tratamento de Erros

Erros 5xx indicam falhas no servidor: **500 Internal Server Error** (aplicação indisponível), **502 Bad Gateway**, **503 Service Unavailable** e **504 Gateway Timeout** (falhas pontuais de infraestrutura). Sua aplicação deve identificar esses códigos e reagendar a requisição após alguns minutos com backoff exponencial. Status dos servidores: [https://status.kobana.com.br](https://status.kobana.com.br).

## Spec OpenAPI

Importe a spec no Postman ou Insomnia para ter uma coleção pronta que sempre reflete a API atual:

- **YAML:** `/api/v1/openapi.yaml`
- **JSON:** `/api/v1/openapi.json`

code.description: Stable error code from the Kobana vocabulary. Do not parse the message — switch on this.

message.description: Human-readable, English. Never includes user-supplied data verbatim.

details.description: Optional, error-specific payload (e.g. `{ required, granted }` on `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`).

error.description: Error envelope. Always present on 4xx and 5xx responses.

ApiV1Error.description: The error envelope every failure answers with: `{ error: { code, message, details? } }`. `code` is a stable UPPER_SNAKE identifier; `details` carries field-level information when there is any.

classification_center.description: The classification center. `name` is `null` if the join is unavailable.

percentage.description: Percentage of the transaction amount, as a number. `null` when the split is amount-driven.

amount.description: Absolute slice in BRL. `null` when the split is percentage-driven.

TransactionClassificationCenterAllocatio.description: How a financial transaction is split across classification centers: one center and its share.

category.description: The category. `name` is `null` if the join is unavailable.

percentage.description: Share of the total, 0–100 with up to 2 decimals. `null` when the row was created amount-only.

amount.description: Allocated amount in BRL. `null` when the row was created percentage-only.

TransactionCategoryAllocationV1.description: How a financial transaction is split across categories (rateio): one category and its share.

custom_classifier.description: The dimension. `name` is `null` if the join is unavailable.

custom_classifier_value.description: Assigned list value (id + label). `null` for scalar dimensions (see `raw_value`) or when the join is unavailable.

raw_value.description: Free value for scalar dimensions; `null` for list dimensions.

percentage.description: Share of the amount as a number. `null` for native single-select assignments.

amount.description: Absolute slice in BRL. `null` for native single-select assignments.

TransactionCustomClassificationV1.description: A custom classifier value applied to a financial transaction.

description.description: Short label written by the user — distinct from `bank_description`.

bank_description.description: Raw description from the bank statement, when imported.

document.description: Document number (NF, boleto, comprovante) that originated this movement.

document_date.description: Issue date of the source document (NF, boleto). Distinct from `occurred_at` (settlement) and `competence_date` (accounting period).

amount.description: A number in BRL, 2 decimal places. Always positive — direction is carried by `type`.

occurred_at.description: When the movement hit the account.

competence_date.description: Accounting period this movement belongs to. Falls back to `occurred_at` when null.

category.description: Primary category (rows[0] of the category rateio). Full split in `category_allocations[]`.

classification_center.description: Primary classification center (rows[0] of the rateio). Full split in `classification_center_allocations[]`.

classification_center_allocations.description: The rateio (split) across classification centers. Empty when there is no split.

category_allocations.description: The rateio (split) across categories. Empty when there is no split.

custom_classifications.description: Custom-classifier assignments (one per dimension for native single-select). Empty when none.

metadata.description: Metadados do sistema, gerenciados pela Kobana. Somente leitura.

custom_metadata.description: Metadados do usuário: objeto JSON livre.

created_via.description: Channel that created the record: `dashboard`, `import`, `api`, `mcp`, `cli` or `other`. On API calls it is the `X-Request-Source` header. `null` when the change came from the system (scheduled jobs) or predates this tracking.

created_via_other.description: App that created the record when the channel is `other` (`X-Request-Source-Other`).

created_by_email.description: E-mail of the person who created the record. `null` for system changes.

updated_via.description: Channel that last changed the record: `dashboard`, `import`, `api`, `mcp`, `cli` or `other`. On API calls it is the `X-Request-Source` header. `null` when the change came from the system (scheduled jobs) or predates this tracking.

updated_via_other.description: App that last changed the record when the channel is `other` (`X-Request-Source-Other`).

updated_by_email.description: E-mail of the person who last changed the record. `null` for system changes.

updated_at.description: Last write. Filterable and sortable — it is the incremental-sync window. Rows predating the column carry their `created_at`, since the real last-write date was never recorded.

FinancialTransactionV1.description: A financial transaction (lançamento): a credit or debit on a financial account, realised or forecast, with its classification.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor. Pass back as `?cursor=…` to fetch the next page. `null` when there is no next page.

FinancialTransactionListMeta.description: Pagination metadata of a financial transactions listing: `next_cursor` to pass as `cursor` for the next page (null on the last).

FinancialTransactionListResponse.description: One page of financial transactions: the records in `data` and the pagination in `meta`.

amount.description: Allocated amount in BRL, in BRL (`"150.00"`). Provide `percentage` and/or `amount`. A JSON number is still accepted for backward compatibility; the string is canonical and is what the reads return.

TransactionClassificationCenterSplitInpu.description: One line of the classification-center split of a financial transaction, as sent on create or update.

percentage.description: Share of the total (0–100). Provide `percentage` and/or `amount`; the missing one is derived from the other. When both are sent they are stored as given and `amount` is what must add up.

amount.description: Allocated amount in BRL. Provide `percentage` and/or `amount`.

TransactionCategorySplitInput.description: One line of the category split (rateio) of a financial transaction, as sent on create or update.

custom_classifier_value.description: Assigned value: `{id}` for an existing value, or `{name}` to find-or-create it under the dimension.

raw_value.description: Free value for a scalar dimension. Use instead of a value id/name.

amount.description: Optional rateio amount in BRL, in BRL. Omit for native single-select.

TransactionCustomClassificationInput.description: A custom classifier value to apply to a financial transaction, as sent on create or update.

company_id.description: Owning company UUID. Must belong to the tenant and match the account's `company_id` (or the account must be workspace-level).

financial_account_id.description: Settlement account UUID. Must belong to the tenant.

document_date.description: Issue date of the source document (ISO 8601). Pass `null` (PATCH) to clear.

amount.description: A number in BRL (up to 13 integer digits, 2 decimals). Always positive — direction is carried by `type`.

occurred_at.description: When the movement hit the account (ISO 8601).

competence_date.description: Accounting period this movement belongs to. Defaults to `occurred_at` when omitted.

type.description: `debit` = money out, `credit` = money in. Drives the polarity for find-or-create on `{name}` fallbacks.

category.description: `{id}` for an existing category, or `{name}` to find-or-create one scoped to (workspace, company) with polarity derived from `type`. Sending both `id` and `name` returns 400. On update, sent without `categories` it replaces a category rateio with this single category.

person.description: `{id}` for an existing person, or `{name}` to find-or-create one with `customer` polarity for credits / `supplier` for debits. Never both.

classification_center.description: `{id}` for an existing classification center, or `{name}` to find-or-create one with `revenue` polarity for credits / `cost` for debits — a center typed `both` matches either; creates with the narrow polarity when no match. Never both.

classification_centers.description: Rateio (split) across classification centers. Replace-all: the array becomes the row's set; an empty array clears it; omit to leave it alone. Effective amounts must sum to `amount` (1-cent tolerance). Each center's polarity must match the transaction `type` (`both` matches either). When present, the single `classification_center` field is ignored and the legacy FK mirrors rows[0].

categories.description: Category rateio. Replace-all set; an empty array clears it (and `category`); omit to leave it alone. Effective amounts must sum to `amount` (tolerance: the larger of 0.01 and 0.005 per row). When present, `category` is ignored and becomes rows[0]; every category must be of type the transaction's `type` (422 otherwise). The cents a percentage leaves go to the last slice sent without an `amount`.

custom_classifications.description: Custom-classifier assignments. Replace-all: the array becomes the row's set; an empty array clears it; omit to leave it alone. One value per dimension for native single-select.

classified.description: Defaults to `false`. Setting `true` marks the row as already-categorised in the UI.

is_pending.description: Defaults to `false`. When `true`, the row is treated as a forecast — excluded from realised-balance and dashboard income/expense aggregates.

FinancialTransactionUpdateRequest.description: Request body to update a financial transaction: send only the fields to change.

city_ibge_code.description: IBGE municipality code. Required by the fiscal registries, which never key by name.

status.description: Raw status. Derive overdue client-side: `status === "pending" AND due_date < today`.

category.description: Related category — the first slice when split; the split lives in `category_allocations[]` on the detail endpoint. `null` when the payable has no category.

financial_account_id.description: Settlement account once paid. `null` while pending or for non-account-bound payments.

expected_account_id.description: Projected settlement account, used by the forecast widgets pre-payment.

payment_method_kind.description: `utility` (concessionária) and `tribute` are payable-only — they never appear on receivables/transactions.

operation_kind.description: Kobana operation axis. `payment` settles an existing document (boleto/tribute/utility/Pix copy-paste); `transfer` sends to a payee you identify (TED/Pix key or bank data). NULL for non-Kobana methods (cash/card/cheque). Payable-only.

payment_approval.description: Read-only mirror of the human payment-approval gate. `null` = **official** (never gated, or already approved) — the bill is on the list. The gate is a per-workspace setting (on by default): when it is on, a payable created through this API starts `pending_approval` and is **hidden from this list until a person approves it in the app** (`GET /payables/{id}` still returns it). `partially_approved` = approved by some of the people the workspace requires, still waiting on the rest (and still hidden). `creation_rejected` = blocked forever (fraud/DDA). The two terminal values carry the `creation_` qualifier because `kobana_status` already uses `approved` and `rejected` for the bank's own decision — the two sets are deliberately disjoint. To **list the approval queue**, filter it explicitly — e.g. `?payment_approval=pending_approval` (or `[in]=pending_approval,creation_rejected`); the gated bills then appear. Read-only: this API never approves or rejects — that stays a human action in the app. Detail-only audit stamps (`approved_at`, `rejected_at`, `rejection_reason`, `payment_source`) live on `GET /payables/{id}`.

document.description: Free-form reference of the source document (e.g. `NF-12345`, `BOL-001`). Populated by the Fintera / CSV importer and matched by the listing `search` and `documentContains` filters. Distinct from `document_number`.

document_number.description: Structured document number — the bare identifier (e.g. `12345`). Mirrors the "Nº de documento" field in the app UI and is the canonical field for manually-entered / edited document numbers. Distinct from the free-form `document`.

installment_number.description: Position within an installment series. `null` for `type=normal`.

total_installments.description: Total positions in the installment series. `null` for `type=normal`.

parcels_amount.description: Aggregate value of the whole installment series ("Total parcelado"), in BRL. Mirrored from Fintera. `null` for non-installment rows. Each parcela carries the series total — its own slice is `amount`.

group_id.description: Links sibling rows of a recurring/installment series. `null` for `type=normal`.

is_reconciled.description: True when matched against a real bank transaction — a 1:1 manual link (`transaction_id` to a non-auto-created transaction) or membership in an n:m reconciliation group. Settling via the normal pay flow (which generates an auto-created transaction) does NOT set this.

attachments_count.description: Number of attachments. Full metadata via `/api/v1/attachments`.

custom_classifications_count.description: Number of custom-classifier assignments. Full list on the detail endpoint.

company_id.description: Owning company UUID. Must belong to the tenant.

amount.description: A number in BRL (up to 13 integer digits, 2 decimals). Always positive — cost polarity is implicit.

competence_date.description: Accounting period (ISO 8601). Defaults to `due_date` when omitted.

type.description: Defaults to `normal`. `recurring` requires `recurrence_period` and stores the series ahead up to the workspace's provisioning horizon (default 12 months) as rows sharing `group_id`; `installment` requires `total_installments` (2–120). A title that belongs to a series keeps its `type`; a standalone `normal` title may become `recurring`.

person.description: `{id}` for an existing person, or `{name}` to find-or-create one with `supplier` polarity, scoped to (workspace, company). Never both.

category.description: `{id}` for an existing category, or `{name}` to find-or-create one with `debit` polarity. Never both. On update, sent without `categories` it replaces a category rateio with this single category.

classification_center.description: `{id}` for an existing classification center, or `{name}` to find-or-create one with `cost` polarity — matches a center typed `cost` or `both`; creates as `cost` when no match. Never both.

financial_account_id.description: Optional pre-set settlement account. Must belong to the tenant and match `company_id`.

document.description: Free-form reference of the source document (e.g. `NF-12345`, `BOL-001`); what the `search` / `documentContains` filters match. Distinct from `document_number`.

document_number.description: Structured document number — the bare identifier (e.g. `12345`). Mirrors the "Nº de documento" field in the app UI; the canonical field for manually-entered document numbers. Distinct from the free-form `document`.

recurrence_period.description: Required for `type=recurring` and rejected for any other type (`weekly` | `biweekly` | `monthly` | `quarterly` | `yearly`).

total_installments.description: Required for `type=installment` and rejected for any other type — number of parcelas (2–120). A title that belongs to a series keeps its `type` and `total_installments`.

classification_centers.description: Rateio. Replace-all set; the server validates Σ against `amount` (0.01 tolerance). Spread across installments.

categories.description: Category rateio. Replace-all set; an empty array clears it (and `category`); omit to leave it alone. Effective amounts must sum to `amount` (tolerance: the larger of 0.01 and 0.005 per row). When present, `category` is ignored and becomes rows[0]; every category must be of type `debit` (422 otherwise). The cents a percentage leaves go to the last slice sent without an `amount`.

tax_charges.description: Withholding/tax charges. Replace-all set. Attached to the first record of a series.

tax_kind.description: Tribute kind. Set with `payment_method_kind = tribute`; the barcode goes in `barcode`.

description.description: Short label written by the user.

ticket_amount.description: "Valor liquidado" — actual amount that hit the bank. May differ from `nominal_amount` due to processor fees. `null` when not applicable.

nominal_amount.description: Computed: `amount + (interest_amount ?? 0) - (discount_amount ?? 0)`. Reproduced per request — not persisted.

person.description: Related person. `null` when the receivable has no person.

category.description: Related category — the first slice when split; the split lives in `category_allocations[]` on the detail endpoint. `null` when the receivable has no category.

parcels_amount.description: Aggregate value of the whole installment series ("Total parcelado"), in BRL. Mirrored from Fintera. `null` for non-installment rows. Each parcela carries the series total — its own slice is `amount`.

is_reconciled.description: True when matched against a real bank transaction — a 1:1 manual link (`transaction_id` to a non-auto-created transaction) or membership in an n:m reconciliation group. Receiving via the normal flow (auto-created transaction) does NOT set this.

kind.description: Which rail the charge was issued on. `null` when never charged.

status.description: **Commercial** axis (`opened`, `paid`, `overdue`, `canceled`, `generation_failed`, …). Free string — Kobana owns the vocabulary and may add values. ⚠️ Do not branch on this alone: an `opened` charge whose registration has not confirmed is not payable. Use `state`.

registration_status.description: **Registration** axis — the state at the financial institution (`pending`, `confirmed`, `skipped`, `rejected`, `failed`). Free string. This is the axis that says whether the charge can be handed to the payer.

state.description: Computed by Finance (not a Kobana field, and not persisted): the two axes above collapsed into the one state to branch on. A terminal commercial state wins; below it the registration decides between `registering` and `registered`. `registered` is the first state in which the charge can be delivered to the payer — before it, a bank slip does not exist at the bank and a Pix has no QR code.

status_updated_at.description: When the charge mirror was last written (ISO 8601).

charge.description: Charge mirror. `null` when never charged — its presence is what "already charged" means. Read-only — populated when a charge is issued, never through the write endpoints.

payable_status.description: Status of the bill this receipt points at, so "I have the proof" and "the bill was settled" can be told apart without a second call. **A receipt does not settle anything** — through the gateway the settlement happens on confirmation, but an uploaded one leaves the bill exactly as it was, which is why `paid_at` and a `pending` here coexist normally. `null` when no bill is linked. Not filterable — it is a join, not a column. ⚠️ `draft` appears here and never on `PayableV1.status`: a draft is reachable by linking one by hand.

financial_account_id.description: Account the money left from, when known.

source.description: `kobana` — captured automatically when the dispatched payment was confirmed. `upload` — a file sent by a person for a payment made outside the system.

status.description: `pending` — the document is still being fetched (normal for a few minutes after confirmation). `available` — reachable through `download_url` or `document_url`. `failed` — the fetch gave up; see `error_message`.

paid_at.description: Date the payment happened. A date column: naive, midnight UTC.

amount.description: Amount paid, in BRL.

payee_name.description: Who received the money. On a captured receipt this is the bill's beneficiary when it has one, falling back to its supplier — a boleto or utility bill carries no beneficiary of its own.

payment_method_kind.description: How the payment settled. The payable set — receipts only exist on the paying side.

external_uid.description: The gateway payment `uid` this receipt was captured from — the same value the payable carries as `kobana_payment_uid`, for correlating against your own gateway data. `null` on an upload.

attachment_id.description: The stored document in the workspace attachment library. `null` while the capture is pending, and also on an `available` row whose format could not be stored — that row is served by `document_url`.

download_url.description: Absolute URL for the stored bytes. `null` when there is no `attachment_id`. ⚠️ It points at the attachments resource, so fetching it needs a token carrying **`finance/attachments`** — `finance/receipts` alone lists receipts but does not download them.

document_url.description: The document at the origin. Populated on a captured receipt, and the only way to reach one whose format the attachment whitelist refuses. Points at a third-party host, not at this API — no Bearer of ours applies.

error_message.description: Why the capture gave up. Only set while `status` is `failed`.

received_at.description: When the confirmation that triggered the capture was observed. `null` on an upload.

kind.description: `service` is an NFS-e (nota de serviço); `product` is an NF-e (nota de produto).

situation.description: Fiscal status as parsed from the document. `authorized` is a valid note; `cancelled` was cancelled at the origin; `unknown` when the source did not carry a determinable status.

completeness.description: `full` when the whole document (items, taxes) was parsed; `summary` when only the header-level résumé is known (e.g. an NF-e known solely by its access-key summary event).

source.description: Where the note entered the workspace. `nfe_io` — captured from the nfe.io provider; `xml_upload` — an XML someone imported; `sefaz` — fetched from SEFAZ by access key.

direction.description: `inbound` is a note received against the workspace's companies (the only kind the app parks here).

access_key.description: The 44-digit fiscal access key (chave de acesso). Digits only.

series.description: Série. `null` on documents that carry none (e.g. most NFS-e).

municipality_code.description: IBGE municipality code of the service (NFS-e). `null` when not applicable.

nature_of_operation.description: Natureza da operação (NF-e). `null` when the document carries none.

competence_date.description: Competência (NFS-e) — the service reference month. `null` when absent.

issuer_name.description: Legal name of the issuer (prestador / emitente).

recipient_name.description: Legal name of the recipient (tomador / destinatário). `null` when the document omits it.

recipient_document.description: Recipient CNPJ/CPF, digits only. `null` when absent.

recipient_state.description: Two-letter UF of the recipient. `null` when absent.

company_id.description: The workspace company this note was linked to (matched by recipient document). `null` when no company matched — the note is parked unlinked.

net_amount.description: Net value after withholdings, as a number. `null` when the document carries no net figure.

payable_count.description: How many of the document's duplicates are linked to a payable (conta a pagar) in the workspace — one generated from the document, or an existing one associated with it.

duplicate_count.description: Number of duplicates (parcelas) the document declares.

xml_attachment_id.description: The stored XML in the workspace attachment library. `null` when no XML is kept (e.g. a summary-only note).

xml_download_url.description: Absolute URL for the stored XML bytes. `null` when there is no `xml_attachment_id`. ⚠️ It points at the attachments resource, so fetching it needs a token carrying `finance/attachments` — `finance/fiscal_documents` alone lists notes but does not download them.

bearerAuth.description: Send `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`. Signed RS256 by the Kobana authorization server (HS512 only against a local development server). Claims = { iss, aud, exp, jti, scope, sub, org }. **`org` is the tenant** — the organization's public id — while `sub` is the person who consented: it picks no data, but caps the token at that person's permissions in the organization (403 `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION`). Pair it with the `X-Workspace-Id` header, which picks the workspace inside that organization.

get.description: Returns a cursor-paginated page of financial accounts for the workspace tied to the token's `sub` claim. Accounts may belong to a specific company or be workspace-level (`company_id` nullable). **The current balance is NOT returned by this listing** — the stored `balance` column is a write-only seed; the real balance is derived from the transactions ledger and will be available on the detail endpoint. Requires scope `finance/accounts` with access level `read`.

schema.description: Filter by owning company UUID. Accepts `[in]=uuid1,uuid2`. Workspace-level accounts (`company_id IS NULL`) are returned only when this filter is omitted.
Account kind. Accepts `[in]=checking,savings`.
Filter by bank UUID. Accepts `[in]` for multi-bank lookups.
Filter by active flag.
Filter by exact account name. Accepts `[in]`.
Field to order by. Default: `sort_by=name&sort_order=asc`.
Order direction. Defaults to `asc`; ignored without `sort_by`.
Page size. Default 25, max 100.
Opaque cursor for the next page. Round-trip `meta.next_cursor` from the previous response.

Comma-separated top-level fields to return, e.g. `fields=description,amount,due_date`. Omit for every field. `id` is always included; naming an object field returns it whole. An unknown name is a 400 whose `details` lists `unknown` and `available`.

parameters.name: X-Workspace-Id
parameters.description: Workspace to act on, as a UUID. The token identifies the organization; this header picks which of its workspaces the request reads or writes. It is checked against the token's organization, so a workspace owned by anyone else answers `UNKNOWN_WORKSPACE` — the same code as one that does not exist. Omitting it answers `WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` (400).

post.description: Creates a financial account. Requires scope `finance/accounts` with access level `write`. `workspace_id` is taken from the token. `company_id` is required (accounts must belong to a company; workspace-level accounts exist from imports but aren't creatable via v1). `balance` is an opening seed (default `0.00`) — it is NOT the live balance (that is computed from transactions and returned on the detail endpoint) and cannot be updated. The bank may be given as `bank_id` (UUID) or `bank_code` (public COMPE/BACEN, e.g. `341`) — not both (400); an unknown code → 422. The response echoes the resolved bank as `bank: { code, name }`. Pass an `X-Idempotency-Key` header on retries.

get.description: Every financial transaction id the token can see. Requires scope `finance/transactions` with access level `read`. Pairs with `?updated_at[gte]=` on the listing. The delta reports what changed; this reports what still exists. A delta can never report a disappearance — the row it would have to describe is gone — so an id that stops appearing here is the only signal that something left. post.description: Dispatches an approved payable to the bank through the Kobana gateway (creates the payment, then envelopes and approves it on the gateway side). Requires scope `finance/payable_dispatches` with access level `write` — the money resource is deliberately **separate** from `finance/payables` (dispatching money is not editing a bill), while a token with no `finance/…` scope needs just the `write` (or `all`) access level. `X-Idempotency-Key` is **required**. The payable must also carry the payment coordinates for its method and a Kobana-mirrored source account. Returns the refreshed payable detail with the execution mirror (`kobana_status`, `kobana_payment_uid`) populated. **Note:** the Kobana sandbox `example_bank` does not execute outbound payments, so the full `confirmed` cycle is only observable against an environment that actually settles.

post.summary: Gerar cobrança de uma conta a receber
post.description:
Issues a **bank slip** or a **Pix charge** on the gateway so the customer has something to pay, and mirrors it onto the receivable. Requires scope `finance/receivable_charges` with access level `write` — the money resource is its own, so a token reaching only `finance/receivables` cannot charge, and `finance/all` with only `read` cannot either. An `X-Idempotency-Key` header is **required**: a duplicate charge is a second debt your customer receives.

⚠️ **The charge in the response is not deliverable yet.** Registration at the institution is asynchronous, so it comes back `charge.state: "registering"` — a bank slip does not exist at the bank yet and a Pix has no `charge.pix_qrcode`. Poll `GET /receivables/{id}` until `charge.state` is `registered` before sending anything to the payer. There is no refresh endpoint on purpose: the mirror is kept current by a background poll and by the gateway's webhook, and a per-call re-read would burn the same hourly request budget the rest of the integration shares.

The two rails differ in what they require of the payer — a bank slip needs their **full address**, a Pix only name and document — and in what must be registered on the gateway account (an agreement vs. a Pix charging account). A missing piece comes back as 422 naming it; a state that forbids charging comes back as 409.

post.summary: Cancelar a cobrança de uma conta a receber
post.description:
Cancels the charge on the gateway. Same guards as issuing it — Requires scope `finance/receivable_charges` with access level `write`, and an `X-Idempotency-Key` header is required.

⚠️ **A 200 does not mean the charge is dead.** A bank slip stops being payable at once, but a Pix cancellation is a *command* the financial institution confirms later — and until it does, your customer can still pay it. Read `charge.state` on the response: `canceled` is done; anything else means the cancellation is still in flight, and the background poll will keep the mirror moving.

Cancelling is also how you unlock the bill: while a charge is live, `PATCH /receivables/{id}` refuses the fields that describe it (amount, due date, payer) and `DELETE` refuses the row — editing here would not re-issue anything, it would only make the record disagree with what the customer holds.

post.description: Creates a single transaction. Requires scope `finance/transactions` with access level `write`. `workspace_id` is always taken from the token, never from the body. `auto_created` and `transfer_id` are always server-controlled — values in the request are ignored. `{name}` accepted as alternative to `{id}` inside the nested `person` / `category` / `classification_center` object, for CSV-importer ergonomics; sending both inside the same object returns 400. Send `classification_centers[]` to split the amount across classification centers (rateio): effective amounts must sum to `amount` (1-cent tolerance) and each center's polarity must match `type` (`both` matches either). When present it supersedes the single `classification_center` field (which then mirrors rows[0]); the full split rides back on every read as `classification_center_allocations[]`. `categories[]` splits it across categories the same way (no polarity check) and rides back as `category_allocations[]`; it supersedes the single `category` field, which mirrors rows[0]. Pass an `X-Idempotency-Key` header on retries to avoid duplicate inserts.

schema.description: Opaque idempotency token (recommended on POST). Same key + same body returns the cached response with `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`. Same key + different body returns 409 conflict. Scoped per workspace; the fingerprint covers the request method, path, and raw body.

parameters.name: X-Workspace-Id
parameters.description: Workspace to act on, as a UUID. The token identifies the organization; this header picks which of its workspaces the request reads or writes. It is checked against the token's organization, so a workspace owned by anyone else answers `UNKNOWN_WORKSPACE` — the same code as one that does not exist. Omitting it answers `WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` (400).
